+# Dependent pull requests
+
+A dependent PR builds on another PR that has not merged yet. This page explains
+how to develop, validate and land such a PR under this repository's actual
+rules: main-target acceptance via the `CI acceptance` `workflow_run` gate, and
+squash merges into `main`. Nothing here weakens any check, authorizes a
+publication, or substitutes for review.
+
+## Develop
+
+Branch from the dependency's head, not from `main`:
+
+```sh
+git fetch origin pull/<base-pr>/head:dep-base
+git switch -c my-feature dep-base
+```
+
+Open the dependent PR against the dependency's branch (if it lives in this
+repository) or keep it in draft targeting `main` and state the dependency in
+the description (`Refs #<base-pr>`, "blocked by #<base-pr>"). Keep each PR
+reviewable on its own; the pull request template (graph impact, tests run,
+live validation, DCO sign-off on every commit) applies to both PRs
+independently.
+
+## Validate
+
+Run the same fixed local checks as any PR (see [development.md](development.md)).
+The project graph explains impact; it does not execute or certify tests.
+
+Distinguish four identities when reading CI evidence:
+
+- **head** — the commit your PR proposes.
+- **base** — the commit the PR merges onto. For a main-target PR, CI runs on
+  the PR *merge snapshot* of head onto base; if base moves, prior evidence
+  describes an older snapshot.
+- **run / attempt** — acceptance requires exact run/attempt/source identity.
+  Evidence is bound to one workflow run and one attempt; a re-run is a new
+  attempt with its own evidence, and re-running an old run does **not** test a
+  new base. Neither does editing the base branch retroactively re-test your
+  PR: only a fresh CI run on the new merge snapshot produces valid evidence.
+
+Distinguish the kinds of assurance:
+
+- **CI vs review.** `CI acceptance`, Dependency Review, DCO and the CodeQL
+  checks are required machine gates on `main`; CODEOWNERS review by the
+  maintainer is a separate, equally required human gate. Green CI never
+  replaces review, and review never replaces CI.
+- **PR evidence vs exact-main release evidence.** `accepted-ci-*` artifacts on
+  a PR attest the PR's merge snapshot. Releases rely on evidence for the exact
+  `main` commit being released; PR-time evidence does not carry over, and this
+  document authorizes no publish step.
+
+## Safe read-only inspection
+
+These commands only read; they never mutate PRs, branches or runs:
+
+```sh
+# Dependency PR state, base/head identity and mergeability
+gh pr view <base-pr> --json state,baseRefName,headRefName,headRefOid,mergeable
+
+# What your PR adds beyond its dependency
+git log --oneline dep-base..my-feature
+git diff dep-base...my-feature
+
+# CI runs and the exact run/attempt behind an evidence artifact
+gh run list --branch my-feature --workflow CI
+gh run view <run-id> --json headSha,runAttempt,conclusion
+gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<run-id>/attempts/<attempt>
+
+# Accepted evidence for a specific run/attempt (read, do not reinterpret)
+gh run download <acceptance-run-id> --name accepted-ci-<run-id>-<attempt>
+```
+
+Treat downloaded artifact contents as candidate-produced data, exactly as the
+acceptance gate does: test output is evidence about a specific run/attempt and
+source identity, not independent re-execution.
+
+## Refresh evidence and review
+
+Whenever the dependency changes, your PR's previous evidence describes a stale
+snapshot. Refresh it:
+
+```sh
+git fetch origin pull/<base-pr>/head
+git rebase --onto FETCH_HEAD dep-base my-feature   # or merge, per preference
+git push --force-with-lease
+```
+
+Pushing a new head triggers a fresh CI run on the new merge snapshot; this is
+the only path to current evidence. Do not re-run an old attempt and present it
+as covering the new base. If the force-push changed meaningful content,
+re-request review — stale approvals should be refreshed, and branch protection
+dismissal rules are not to be worked around.
+
+Remember the obligation rule: a PR cannot erase its own base obligations. If
+the dependency retires a test declaration, keep existing test IDs through the
+dependent PR and remove old tests only in a subsequent change.
+
+## Merge
+
+Merge order is strict: the dependency merges first (squash into `main`), then
+retarget the dependent PR to `main` if it was stacked on the dependency's
+branch:
+
+```sh
+gh pr edit <dependent-pr> --base main
+```
+
+Because the dependency was squash-merged, rebase the dependent branch onto the
+new `main` so its diff contains only its own changes. The retarget/rebase
+produces a new merge snapshot, so all required checks (`CI acceptance`,
+Dependency Review, DCO, CodeQL) must pass again on that snapshot, and
+maintainer review applies to the final diff. Only then squash-merge the
+dependent PR. Release steps, if any, follow docs/release-policy.md separately
+against the exact `main` commit — never as part of a PR merge.

+# Dependent pull requests
+
+A dependent PR builds on another PR that has not merged yet. This repository
+targets `main`, squash-merges, and accepts changes only through `CI acceptance`
+plus review. None of that changes for dependent work — this page explains how
+to develop, validate, refresh and merge a stack without weakening any gate.
+
+## Develop
+
+Branch the dependent PR from the head of its base PR:
+
+```sh
+git fetch origin
+git switch -c feature-b origin/feature-a
+```
+
+Open the PR against the base PR's branch (not `main`) while the base PR is
+open, so reviewers see only the incremental diff. Every commit still needs a
+DCO sign-off (`git commit -s`), and the PR template (graph impact, tests run,
+live validation) applies to the dependent PR on its own merits.
+
+When the base PR squash-merges, its branch commits never land on `main` as-is.
+Retarget the dependent PR to `main` and rebase onto the squash commit:
+
+```sh
+git fetch origin main
+git rebase --onto origin/main feature-a feature-b
+```
+
+## Head, base, run and attempt
+
+- **Head**: the dependent branch's tip commit — what CI actually tested.
+- **Base**: the commit the PR merges into (the base PR's head while stacked,
+  then `main` after retargeting).
+- **Run**: one execution of the `CI` workflow for a specific merge snapshot.
+- **Attempt**: a re-run of that run. Acceptance requires exact run/attempt and
+  source identity; a re-run or a base change does **not** automatically test a
+  new base. A changed base means a new merge snapshot, which needs a fresh CI
+  run and fresh acceptance — never assume prior evidence transfers.
+
+## Validate
+
+Run the same fixed checks locally that CI runs (see
+[development.md](development.md)); the graph explains impact but never
+replaces mandatory validation. Safe, read-only inspection commands:
+
+```sh
+# What the dependent PR adds beyond its base PR
+git log --oneline origin/feature-a..feature-b
+git diff origin/feature-a...feature-b
+
+# Confirm the recorded head/base of the PR and its check runs
+gh pr view <number> --json headRefOid,baseRefName,baseRefOid
+gh pr checks <number>
+
+# Inspect the exact run/attempt behind a check
+gh run view <run-id> --json headSha,status,conclusion,attempt
+gh run download <run-id> --name accepted-ci-<run-id>-<attempt>
+```
+
+These commands read state; they do not approve, publish or rerun anything.
+
+## CI vs review
+
+CI evidence and review are separate obligations. Passing `CI acceptance`,
+Dependency Review, DCO and the CodeQL checks never substitutes for CODEOWNERS
+review, and an approval never substitutes for the required checks. Both must
+hold on the PR's **current** head: pushing a rebase or new commits invalidates
+stale review and requires fresh CI on the new merge snapshot.
+
+## PR evidence vs exact-main release evidence
+
+`accepted-ci-<run>-<attempt>` artifacts attest the merge snapshot CI actually
+ran — candidate-produced data validated for exact run/attempt/source identity.
+They are **not** release evidence. Release and other exact-main actions rely on
+acceptance for the exact `main` commit produced by the squash merge, which is a
+different commit than any PR snapshot. After merging the base PR, the dependent
+PR's earlier evidence describes an obsolete base; it cannot be reused.
+
+## Refresh evidence and review
+
+After the base PR merges:
+
+1. Retarget the dependent PR to `main` and rebase onto the squash commit.
+2. Resolve conflicts locally and re-run the fixed local checks.
+3. Push; CI runs on the new merge snapshot and `CI acceptance` re-validates.
+4. Request fresh review for the new head.
+
+Keep base obligations intact: a PR cannot erase its own base obligations, and
+retiring a test declaration still keeps the test ID until a subsequent change.
+
+## Merge
+
+Merge order is strict: the base PR merges first, the dependent PR only after
+retargeting, fresh CI acceptance on its new head/base, and fresh review. Main
+protection (`CI acceptance`, Dependency Review, DCO, CodeQL) applies unchanged.
+Squash-merge the dependent PR as usual.
+

+structure stand in for evidence. When in doubt, treat the dependent PR as an
+ordinary PR against `main` with extra bookkeeping about whose head it was
+built on.

+A dependent PR builds on another PR that has not merged yet. This repository
+targets `main` with squash merges and exact-identity CI acceptance, so stacked

+- **Base**: the branch the PR targets. For a dependent PR during development
+  this may be the parent PR's branch; before final acceptance it must be
+  retargeted to `main` (only `main` is protected and releasable).

+  Acceptance requires exact run/attempt/source identity; evidence from one

+  substitutes for the other.

+

+
+1. Branch from the parent PR's head so you can build on its changes:
+

+   git fetch origin
+   git switch -c my-feature parent-feature
+   ```
+
+2. Keep commits signed off (`git commit -s`) — DCO checks every commit.
+3. Open the PR against the parent branch *or* against `main` as draft. Either
+   way, state the dependency ("Depends on #N") in the description.
+

+

+[development.md](development.md)); local journals and receipts are
+diagnostics, not trusted CI attestations:

+```sh
+uv run --project packages/python python -m tools.development sync all
+uv run --project packages/python python -m tools.development run graph --check-id graph

+git fetch origin
+git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
+git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat
+
+# Confirm ancestry: is the parent PR's head contained in yours / in main?
+git merge-base --is-ancestor <parent-head-sha> HEAD && echo contained
+git merge-base --is-ancestor <parent-head-sha> origin/main && echo merged
+
+# Inspect runs and evidence without executing anything:
+gh pr view <number> --json baseRefName,headRefOid,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup
+gh run list --workflow CI --branch <branch>
+gh run view <run-id> --json headSha,runAttempt,conclusion
+gh run download <run-id> --name accepted-ci-<run-id>-<attempt>
+```
+
+Graph reports (`project-graph` artifacts, `impact.json`, `explorer.html`) are
+bounded context for impact review; graph coverage is never execution evidence.
+

+
+CI evidence is bound to an exact run/attempt and source identity. When the
+parent PR is updated or merged:
+

+  new head, a new merge snapshot, and a fresh `CI` run. A base edit — or a
+  rerun of an old run — does **not** automatically test your PR against the
+  new base; only a new run on the updated merge snapshot does, and only its
+  own `accepted-ci-*` artifact attests it.

+  should see the post-rebase state, especially where squash-merging the parent
+  rewrote the shared history.

+  keep existing test IDs while retiring declarations, and remove old tests in

+
+1. Wait for the parent PR to squash-merge into `main`.
+2. Retarget your PR to `main` (if it targeted the parent branch, GitHub
+   usually retargets automatically when the parent branch is deleted — verify
+   with `gh pr view --json baseRefName`).
+3. Rebase onto `origin/main`. Because the parent squash-merged, your branch
+   still carries the parent's original commits; drop them so only your own
+   changes remain:
+
+   ```sh
+   git fetch origin
+   git rebase --onto origin/main <parent-head-sha> my-feature
+   ```
+

+   acceptance` plus the other required checks (Dependency Review, DCO, the
+   Python, TypeScript and Actions CodeQL checks) and maintainer review.
+5. Squash-merge. Keep the sign-off intact in the squash commit message.
+

+
+- It never skips, weakens, or substitutes for required checks or review.
+- It never treats missing/skipped/stale/failed evidence as a pass.
+- It never authorizes a release or publication: releases are cut from `main`
+  only, after acceptance passes on the exact main revision, through the
+  dedicated release workflows.

+  retested a dependent PR against the new base.

+
+A dependent PR builds on another PR that has not merged yet. This page explains
+how to develop, validate and land such stacks under this repository's actual
+rules: every PR ultimately targets `main`, acceptance validates exact-run
+evidence, and merges are squashed. Nothing here weakens any required check.

+- **Head** — the exact commit under test (`github.event.pull_request.head.sha`

+  builds from head and base).

+  PR during development this is the parent PR's branch; at acceptance time the
+  base that matters is `main`.
+- **Run** — one execution of the `CI` workflow; `CI acceptance` validates one
+  specific run by ID.
+- **Attempt** — a re-run of the same run ID. Acceptance binds to the exact
+  run/attempt pair; evidence from another attempt does not transfer.
+
+A key consequence: **editing or advancing a base does not automatically test a
+new combination**. If the parent PR changes, or `main` moves, your dependent
+PR's previous CI evidence describes an older snapshot. Rebase or update the
+branch so a fresh run tests the combination you actually intend to merge; do
+not assume a rerun of an old run revalidates the new base.
+
+## Developing a stack
+
+1. Branch the dependent work from the parent PR's branch.
+2. Open the dependent PR against the parent branch (or as a draft against
+   `main` clearly marked as blocked) so reviewers see only the incremental
+   diff.
+3. Keep each commit signed off (`git commit -s`); DCO checks every commit.
+4. Run the same fixed local checks described in [development.md](development.md);
+   local journals and receipts are diagnostics, not trusted CI attestations.
+
+Safe, read-only inspection commands while working on a stack:
+
+```sh
+# What the dependent PR adds beyond its parent (no checkout, no execution):
+git log --oneline parent-branch..dependent-branch
+git diff parent-branch...dependent-branch
+
+# Confirm what base a PR currently declares:
+gh pr view <number> --json baseRefName,headRefName,headRefOid,mergeStateStatus
+
+# Inspect CI runs and their head SHAs without rerunning anything:
+gh run list --workflow CI --branch dependent-branch \
+  --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion
+gh run view <run-id> --json headSha,runAttempt,conclusion
+
+# Bounded impact view for the stacked change:
+uv run --project packages/python python -m tools.project_graph \
+  --output .project-graph/impact.json report --base <base-sha> --head <head-sha>
+```
+
+These commands read state; none of them approve, publish or merge anything.
+
+## CI versus review
+
+CI (`CI`, `CI acceptance`, Dependency Review, DCO, and the Python, TypeScript
+and Actions CodeQL checks) is required on `main` by branch protection, and
+acceptance requires exact run/attempt/source identity, all base and proposed
+job obligations, the trusted registry, and every declared journey test in
+every mapped lane. Review is a separate, equally mandatory gate: CODEOWNERS
+routes every change to the maintainer, and contract/workflow paths are always
+maintainer-reviewed. Green CI does not substitute for review, and an approval
+does not substitute for accepted CI. A parent PR's approval or green run never
+carries over to a dependent PR — each PR earns both independently against the
+snapshot it actually merges.
+
+## PR evidence versus exact-main release evidence
+
+- **PR evidence**: the `CI` run on the PR merge snapshot plus the
+  `accepted-ci-<run>-<attempt>` artifact. It attests that *that snapshot*
+  passed; test output remains candidate-produced data the gate does not
+  independently reexecute.

+  the main-ancestry check. Because merges are squashed, the merged commit on
+  `main` is a *new* SHA; PR evidence never doubles as release evidence, and
+  passing PR CI does not authorize publication. Releases remain a separate,
+  maintainer-driven process.

+Squash merging rewrites history: when the parent PR merges, its branch commits
+are replaced on `main` by a single new commit. For the dependent PR:
+
+1. Wait for the parent to merge to `main`.
+2. Retarget the dependent PR to `main` (GitHub often does this automatically
+   when the parent branch is deleted — verify with

+   commits (`git rebase --onto main parent-branch dependent-branch`), keeping

+   `CI` run and a fresh `CI acceptance` result are required, and stale review
+   approvals should be re-requested since the reviewed diff context changed.

+is bound to an exact run/attempt/source identity, so there is no shortcut.

+  declarations while deleting their tests in the same change — keep existing
+  test IDs while retiring declarations, then remove the old tests in a

+- Treat a re-run of an old run, or a base-branch edit, as testing the new
+  base combination.

+  evidence and are out of scope for PR flow entirely.
